decision: Make WorkerRuntime retain the exact per-claim lease fencing token and require it for heartbeat, complete, and fail mutations.
problem: MissionQueue supports requireLeaseToken=true, but WorkerRuntime previously discarded the token returned by claim and called heartbeat/complete/fail without it. That made the normal worker abstraction incompatible with the fencing contract required before distributed/Qubes workers.

correctness.preferred: Runtime-owned per-mission lease token state, captured from claim and supplied on every owned mutation.
correctness.reason: Worker/session identity alone cannot distinguish an old execution from a later reclaim using the same identity. The claim token is the actual fencing authority.

robustness_security.preferred: Fail closed when the runtime does not hold a token; prove an old runtime is rejected after the same worker/session identity reclaims the mission with a new token.
robustness_security.reason: This prevents stale completions, heartbeats, or failures from being accepted merely because a worker name/session string was reused.

latency_resources_regression.preferred: Keep the token in an in-memory Map scoped to the WorkerRuntime instance and reuse the existing coordinator mutation calls.
latency_resources_regression.reason: Adds no filesystem, network, qrexec, or Qubes round trips and only constant-size local state per active mission. It has a smaller regression surface than adding a second durable worker-session store.

alternatives_rejected: Worker/session identity only: insufficient fencing when the same identity is reused after reclaim.
Pass lease tokens manually through every caller instead of WorkerRuntime owning them: makes the abstraction easy to misuse and leaves runOnce unable to enforce the contract centrally.
Disable requireLeaseToken in WorkerRuntime paths: weakens the security/reliability control needed for distributed workers.
Persist runtime lease tokens in a new database/store: unnecessary for Slice 1; process restart should lose local authority and reacquire through the durable coordinator.
qa: runOnce under requireLeaseToken=true carries the exact claim token through heartbeat and completion.
Execution failure under requireLeaseToken=true persists through fail using the held token and remains retryable under queue policy.
Two runtimes using the same workerId and same sessionId receive different tokens after restart/reclaim; the old runtime is rejected and the new runtime completes.
Missing local lease authority fails closed rather than falling back to identity-only mutation.
failure_lessons: Adding fencing to MissionQueue is insufficient if the higher-level WorkerRuntime silently drops the fencing credential.
A stable worker identity is useful for observability, not for stale-execution fencing; ownership generations need a per-claim token.
Process restart should not preserve local lease authority by default. A restarted worker must recover/reclaim through durable state and receive a fresh token.

resource_impact.memory: one lease-token entry per active mission in the WorkerRuntime instance

remaining_risks: The filesystem persistence/lock remains same-host only.
Slice 1 still needs independent executable QA; hosted runner provisioning remains a separate blocker.
Qubes transport must preserve these lease-token semantics end-to-end in Slice 2 before REAL-WORKER readiness.
